ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ passes through the midpoint A of the hypotenuse of the right triangle $\triangle BOC$, and intersects with BC at point D. Given that the area of $\triangle BOD$ is 21, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct $AE\perp$ to the $x$-axis, then the area of $\triangle AOE$ and $\triangle DOC$ is $\frac{1}{2}|k|$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of the quadrilateral $BAEC$ and $\triangle BOD$ is $21$, \\
$\because$ $AE\perp x$ axis, \\
$\angle BCO=90^\circ$, and point A is the midpoint of OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOE = \angle BOC$, \\
$\angle AEO = \angle BCO = 90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOE \sim \triangle BOC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AOE}}{{S}_{\triangle BOC}} = \left(\frac{OA}{OB}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\because$ the area of quadrilateral $BAEC$ times the area of $\triangle AOE$ equals the area of $\triangle BOC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AOE}}{{S}_{\text{quadrilateral }BAEC}} = \frac{{S}_{\triangle AOE}}{21} = \frac{1}{3}$, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AOE} = 7$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}|k| = 7$, \\
Solving for $k$, we get: $k = \pm 14$, \\
$\because$ the inverse proportion function passes through the first quadrant, \\
$\therefore$ $k = \boxed{14}$.

method.method_draft: Area-ratio and hyperbola-area route. From the image, view triangle BOC as a right triangle with right angle at C, D on side BC, and A on hypotenuse OB; drop AE perpendicular to the x-axis. From the text, A is the midpoint of OB and lies on y=k/x. Because A is halfway along OB, triangles AOE and BOC are similar with linear ratio 1:2, so area(AOE)=1/4 area(BOC). For any point (x,y) on y=k/x in the first quadrant, the right triangle formed with the coordinate axes has area xy/2=k/2, so area(AOE)=k/2. Likewise, since D is on the same hyperbola and C is its foot on the x-axis, area(DOC)=k/2. Therefore area(DOC)=area(AOE)=1/4 area(BOC). Segment OD partitions triangle BOC into triangles BOD and DOC, so area(BOD)=area(BOC)-area(DOC)=3/4 area(BOC)=21. Thus area(BOC)=28, area(AOE)=7, and k/2=7, giving k=14; the first-quadrant placement gives the positive sign.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中有坐标轴，O 为原点，C 在 x 轴正半轴上，BC 是竖直线段，B 在 C 的上方，所以三角形 BOC 在 C 处为直角，OB 是斜边。点 A 位于斜边 OB 上，题意给出 A 是 OB 的中点。曲线 y=k/x 位于第一象限，经过 A，并与竖直边 BC 交于 D。推理：按方法作 AE 垂直于 x 轴，E 为垂足。因为 A 是 OB 的中点，所以 OA/OB=1/2。又因为 OE 与 OC 都在 x 轴方向，AE 与 BC 都垂直于 x 轴，所以 ∠AEO=∠BCO=90°，且 ∠AOE=∠BOC，因此 △AOE ∼ △BOC，面积比为 (OA/OB)^2=(1/2)^2=1/4。设 S_{BOC}=S，则 S_{AOE}=S/4。由于 A 在 y=k/x 上，若 A=(x_A,y_A)，则 x_A y_A=k，所以 S_{AOE}=x_A y_A/2=k/2。D 也在 y=k/x 上，且 D 在 BC 上，C 是其到 x 轴的垂足，因此 S_{DOC}=k/2。于是 S_{DOC}=S_{AOE}=S/4。线段 OD 将 △BOC 分成 △BOD 和 △DOC，所以 S_{BOD}=S-S/4=3S/4。已知 S_{BOD}=21，因此 3S/4=21，得 S=28。于是 S_{AOE}=S/4=7，又 S_{AOE}=k/2，所以 k/2=7，解得 k=14。曲线在第一象限，故 k 为正。

method.CoT_answer_check_final: 图像描述：图中有坐标轴，O 为原点，C 在 x 轴正半轴上，BC 是竖直线段，B 在 C 的上方，所以三角形 BOC 在 C 处为直角，OB 是斜边。点 A 位于斜边 OB 上，题意给出 A 是 OB 的中点。曲线 y=k/x 位于第一象限，经过 A，并与竖直边 BC 交于 D。推理：按方法作 AE 垂直于 x 轴，E 为垂足。因为 A 是 OB 的中点，所以 OA/OB=1/2。又因为 OE 与 OC 都在 x 轴方向，AE 与 BC 都垂直于 x 轴，所以 ∠AEO=∠BCO=90°，且 ∠AOE=∠BOC，因此 △AOE ∼ △BOC，面积比为 (OA/OB)^2=(1/2)^2=1/4。设 S_{BOC}=S，则 S_{AOE}=S/4。由于 A 在 y=k/x 上，若 A=(x_A,y_A)，则 x_A y_A=k，所以 S_{AOE}=x_A y_A/2=k/2。D 也在 y=k/x 上，且 D 在 BC 上，C 是其到 x 轴的垂足，因此 S_{DOC}=k/2。于是 S_{DOC}=S_{AOE}=S/4。线段 OD 将 △BOC 分成 △BOD 和 △DOC，所以 S_{BOD}=S-S/4=3S/4。已知 S_{BOD}=21，因此 3S/4=21，得 S=28。于是 S_{AOE}=S/4=7，又 S_{AOE}=k/2，所以 k/2=7，解得 k=14。曲线在第一象限，故 k 为正。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ passes through the midpoint A of the hypotenuse of the right triangle $\triangle BOC$, and intersects with BC at point D. Given that the area of $\triangle BOD$ is 21, what is the value of $k$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct $AE\perp$ to the $x$-axis, then the area of $\triangle AOE$ and $\triangle DOC$ is $\frac{1}{2}|k|$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of the quadrilateral $BAEC$ and $\triangle BOD$ is $21$, \\
$\because$ $AE\perp x$ axis, \\
$\angle BCO=90^\circ$, and point A is the midpoint of OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOE = \angle BOC$, \\
$\angle AEO = \angle BCO = 90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOE \sim \triangle BOC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AOE}}{{S}_{\triangle BOC}} = \left(\frac{OA}{OB}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\because$ the area of quadrilateral $BAEC$ times the area of $\triangle AOE$ equals the area of $\triangle BOC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AOE}}{21} = \frac{1}{3}$, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AOE} = 7$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}|k| = 7$, \\
Solving for $k$, we get: $k = \pm 14$, \\
$\because$ the inverse proportion function passes through the first quadrant, \\
$\therefore$ $k = \boxed{14}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, O is at the coordinate origin, OC goes right along the positive x-axis, CB is a vertical line segment, and point B is directly above C, so triangle BOC is right-angled at C. Segment OB is the hypotenuse, and point A lies on OB and the problem statement indicates that it is the midpoint of the hypotenuse. The curve y=k/x is located in the first quadrant, passes through A, and intersects the vertical side BC at point D.

Reasoning: By the coordinate parameter method, let C=(a,0), B=(a,b), where a>0 and b>0. Because A is the midpoint of the hypotenuse OB, A=(a/2,b/2). Also A lies on the hyperbola y=k/x, so k=(a/2)(b/2)=ab/4.

Point D lies on BC, so its x-coordinate is a; at the same time D lies on y=k/x, so the y-coordinate of D is k/a=(ab/4)/a=b/4, that is, D=(a,b/4). Therefore the length of BD is b-b/4=3b/4. Taking BD as the base, the distance from point O to the line BC (that is, x=a) is a, so the area of triangle BOD is (1/2)*a*(3b/4)=3ab/8.

It is known that the area of triangle BOD is 21, so 3ab/8=21, giving ab=56. Therefore k=ab/4=56/4=14. Also, the hyperbola in the figure is in the first quadrant, so k>0, and the answer is 14.
